item.text: {"question_id":"6B.4","answer":"The supplied evidence shows some Lula-government institutional staffing and service mobilization, but it does not establish that administrators were qualified and retained, that staffing and resources were adequate across social services, or that procurement was transparent. The National Education Council had a formal 2023 composition and produced education standards, while the Novo PAC created interministerial qualification, procurement, and program-management bodies; these demonstrate institutional structures, not implementation competence, retention, resource adequacy, or service performance (BATCH-0006-E002; BATCH-0018-E006). In the Yanomami response, the federal government reported deploying 765 health professionals, reopening seven health posts, establishing a reference center, and supplying medicines and food, but the figures were government-reported, did not establish quality or equitable access, and the crisis remained ongoing (BATCH-0013-E004). Contrary evidence includes TCU findings of weak monitoring in social-assistance programs, inadequate supervision and municipal support, insufficient household verification, deficient planning for education-professional training, and possible impairment of sanitation-framework implementation (BATCH-0005-E003; BATCH-0003-E009; BATCH-0005-E007; BATCH-0005-E008). The supplied procurement material concerns a TCU audit of military overseas purchases and general alerts about possible nontransparent resource use; it provides no welfare-specific evidence of procurement competition, contract performance, or corruption findings (BATCH-0014-E001; BATCH-0005-E012). Attribution is generally institutional or ministerial rather than personally attributable to Lula.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0006-E002","BATCH-0018-E006","BATCH-0013-E004"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0005-E003","BATCH-0003-E009","BATCH-0005-E007","BATCH-0005-E008","BATCH-0014-E001","BATCH-0005-E012"],"limitations_and_gaps":["No supplied evidence directly establishes administrator qualifications, retention, salaries, staffing ratios, or broad adequacy of social-service resources.","No supplied evidence demonstrates welfare-specific procurement competition, contract performance, or procurement corruption findings.","Institutional outputs and government-reported deployment figures do not establish implementation quality or outcomes.","Attribution is usually to federal ministries, councils, or subnational administrations rather than Lula personally; the evidence is limited to 2023 and several findings concern inherited or ongoing programs."],"corrections_made":["Removed security-personnel evidence as irrelevant to ordinary social-service administration.","Recast council creation, procurement bodies, and Yanomami deployment as evidence of institutional action or mobilization, not proof of qualified staffing or professional competence.","Made the absence of welfare-specific procurement evidence explicit.","Preserved the TCU findings, attribution limits, period fit, and uncertainty."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Direct evidence is needed on qualifications, retention, staffing adequacy, budgets and resource execution across social services.","Welfare-specific procurement records, competition, contract monitoring, and audit findings are missing.","Evidence of later correction, service quality, and outcomes would clarify whether institutional structures translated into competent delivery."]}
